record.paper_title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
record.original_question: For spectral postprocessing of HDG methods, determine—by importing the techniques behind Theorem 5.1 and comparing with the mixed-method construction in [49]—what was missing either from the earlier HDG approach or from the HDG methods it studied, so that one could achieve convergence order 2k+2 instead of only 2k+1.

evidence.quote: Spectral postprocessing. In [ 67 ], a similar approach for HDG methods could only provide an order of convergence of 2k+1. One wonders if by applying the techniques leading to Theorem 5.1 to what was done in [ 49 ] for mixed methods, one could identify what was missing in the approach used, or in the HDG methods considered, in [ 67 ] to obtain order 2k+2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order elliptic eigenvalue problem
  -Δu = λ u in Ω,   u = 0 on ∂Ω,
on a bounded polyhedral domain Ω ⊂ ℝ^d, discretized by a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method on a shape-regular simplicial mesh of size h. Let k ≥ 0 be the polynomial degree used to approximate the scalar variable u, the flux q = -∇u, and the numerical trace on element interfaces. Denote by (λ_h, u_h, q_h) the HDG eigenpair approximations.

It is known that for sufficiently smooth eigenfunctions the eigenvalue error |λ - λ_h| converges at rate h^{2k+1}. A spectral (Rayleigh-quotient–type) postprocessing applied locally to (u_h, q_h) has been shown for mixed methods (such as the Brezzi–Douglas–Marini method) to produce a postprocessed eigenvalue approximation λ_h^* satisfying |λ - λ_h^*| = O(h^{2k+2}); the same enhancement has been obtained for HDG only at rate h^{2k+1}.

Problem. Identify a structural ingredient — either an additional property required of the HDG method (for instance, of the underlying projection / numerical-trace stabilization), or an enrichment of the spectral postprocessing procedure — that, when imposed, allows one to prove
  |λ - λ_h^*| = O(h^{2k+2})
for the HDG spectral postprocessing, matching the rate available for mixed methods. Equivalently, determine what was missing in the previous HDG spectral-postprocessing analysis or in the family of HDG methods considered there, so as to bridge the order gap from 2k+1 to 2k+2.
artifact.category_tag: HDG methods for elliptic eigenvalue problems
artifact.status_search_result: The improved 2k+2 spectral postprocessing rate is established for mixed methods (BDM) and partially for some HDG settings, but the question of identifying precisely what is missing in the general HDG spectral-postprocessing analysis to consistently reach order 2k+2 instead of 2k+1 is posed as an open problem. No published resolution closing this specific gap was found.

status_evidence.title: Spectral approximations by the HDG method
status_evidence.snippet: A Rayleigh quotient-like formula applied to certain locally postprocessed approximations can yield eigenvalues that converge faster at the rate 2k+2 for the HDG method as well as for the BDM method.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier HDG spectral postprocessing achieves rate 2k+2 only in restricted settings; the general gap motivates the open question.

status_evidence.title: An adjoint-based super-convergent Galerkin approximation of eigenvalues
status_evidence.claim: Related superconvergence techniques exist but do not directly resolve the HDG order gap identified.
